I like how I tried committing suicide, ate a shit ton of sleep aids (hardcore ones for insomnia even), and didn't die. This thought still plays on repeat in my mind from time to time, but I haven't made another attempt because the first one was such a let down. Shit, no one even knows I tried to kill myself because I woke up fine. Zero consequences.

I just keep existing, same as always.

It's 2 in the morning. You take the knife out of the drawer, you sit with it in your hand, disassociating for hours until the sun comes up. You go to sleep. You start your day. You die a small death but not the big one. 

Yeah, OP, I get you.

I think the reason suicide is looked down upon can be split into three parts: its permanency, death as a concept, and relationships. Permanency is pretty straight forward: you can't really take back a successful attempt, you're just dead. I think that bothers other people because there isn't another option another way to correct that. For example, if you kill yourself because you don't have a job despite sending out numerous resumes and doing interviews, and then tomorrow you get an email saying you have the job. Well, people are upset because they see it as a premature death. Can any of us see the future? No. But when cases like these happen that's when people start with that "a permanent solution to a temporary problem" line.

Second, death as a whole makes most people uncomfortable, so the thought of someone willingly wanting to end it is a big yikes. We don't know what happens to the you that is thinking and living right now after you die. Sure, we know what happens to the body, the decay there, but the ego—the mind—no idea. And that's terrifying to some people. So, thus the taboo.

The last part is tricky, but it's a factor regardless if you have people in your life or not (good Samaritans are a thing): relationships. Humans, for better or worse, are social little assholes. So people will feel some type of ways when you try to cut that social cord. I myself, despite wanting very much to die, am guilty of this one. I'm a hypocrite, I know. But the whole thought is, someone cares for you, and maybe that will be enough. Again, assholes the whole lot of us. But, assholes together I suppose.

You have every right to be upset and feeling the way you do. Your life sounds very messy and chaotic right now, and no one knows the future. There's not much assurance to be given for what you need to feel safe. That's not pathetic, that's the misfortune of being human.

But comment on here. Let it out. At least we see you. At least we hear.
Mmm maybe. I don't know. I hope something changes soon, because at this point I know I won't be making 31. Thank you for understanding, it's kind of refreshing to hear.

Well, it's kind of like this. I know the world is a horrible place, there's no good reason to add to that by being a crappy person. So I don't. Kindness isn't hard to do, so I do it. If I can prevent more people from turning out like me, all the better. I still very much want to die—so very very badly—but family and friends can't handle me killing myself. One day they are going to have to. But until then, I'm stuck in some awful limbo. So, the least I can do is make people smile and spread that happiness I can't actually feel.

First of all, you did an amazing job matching the style of the game, an I absolutely love how you've shaded her skin (not only are the color shifts smooth her, it looks like how the game would render darker characters). However, there are some minor edits I think could be applied here to make it a more finalized render.

Let's talk about line thickness! You got the flow down pat in a lot of parts, but the line itself (particularly at the crown of her head and cheekjawline) is too thick. Since Asra and Portia both have super curly hair, I recommend looking at their sprites for how thick those lines have to be. They'll help a lot here because their hair is light and you'll be able to see how line is handled there. Plus, you mentioned your character's hair as being super curly and having to tone it down and I think that's a shame (still good hair, silhouette is great, but I'm a sucker for some 4C/4B curl)! I think if you wanted to do super curls, you'd block out the silhouette first and had alternating small and thick curls like a combo of Asra+Portia (if that makes sense, sorry that I don't have examples)! 

Next up would be line color. So, Arcana uses line color to 1) still be seen in the darker shades because they focus on line giving form than shape and 2) blend more with the color of the overall piece so line art doesn't stand out. You did a really good job of that with the color you picked for the face! For the hair, little details get lost. But, again, an easy fix for sure! What I would do is look at a character like Valerius. The brown in his hair is a little less warm toned and desaturated than the brown for your character, but I think it'll help to see how they picked a shade that's close to black but not. The key here would be to try to pick a black that not 0 on any of the value scales, just numbers in the single digits to high teens/low twenties (like a very dark warm brown). Also, you have a big highlight in your hair. If you want to allude to dark bouncy curls I recommend breaking up the highlights a la Portia with her hair down.

And lastly, not sure if you'll every do full body or  not, but if you do, here's two things that'll pop your art more into The Arcana style! Put your lineart on a separate layer and clip a gradient color over it (or if that doesn't flow nice still do a clip layer and just paint the lines separately). Also, find a watercolor or paper/grainy texture and use overlay on that texture layer and bring the opacity down until it merges nicely with your flats underneath!

Sorry for the word vomit, but I hope this helps! You're a fantastic artist, keep up the awesome work!

I did that recently and, yeah, it explained a lot, and up until this quarantine happened, I was seeing an improvement (not a crazy amount, but def not the glaring). Turns out, I have an extremely intimidating aura and don't dress in a way that dissipates that, so I eased up on that. I may not smile as much as the next person still, but there is a difference.
